query: Why do some agents have longer resolution times?

per_column.name: assigned_resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether the assigned agent matches the closer is a genuine axis relevant to resolution-time analysis (hand-offs may lengthen resolution). Derivable from assigned_to vs closed_by present in original table; values are a sound reading.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents gives a strong grouping axis for comparing resolution times across issue types. Well grounded in short_description (e.g. 'access the database' -> database, 'VPN issue' -> vpn). Partly redundant with existing category column but more granular/derived from text.

per_column.name: incident_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Severity (outage/degraded/access_denied) is a plausible driver of resolution time and a useful axis. Mostly grounded, but 'Unable to access the database' -> 'access_denied' is a reasonable read while some assignments (e.g. degraded for 'frequent disconnection') are inferential; NULLs for silent rows are appropriate. Some values assert severity the terse text only weakly supports.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Failure mode is a genuine new axis for modeling resolution time. Grounded for cases like 'connection unstable' -> connection_failure, but 'Unable to access the database' -> connection_failure is a specific inference the text does not clearly support (could be permissions), indicating some overconfident labeling.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs office/department-wide) is a strong candidate driver of resolution time. However most short_descriptions are silent on scope, yet 280 rows are labeled 'individual_user' as a confident default — that asserts specifics the text does not state. Unknown values for silent rows would be correct; the default weakens groundedness.

per_column.name: is_ticket_unresolved
per_column.rationale: Largely derivable from state/closed_at and is nearly constant (478 false / 22 true), and partly redundant with the original state column, giving limited analytical leverage for comparing agent resolution times. Grounded where derived, but low-variance.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine new grouping/modeling axes (category, severity, failure_mode, resolver_match, scope) directly relevant to explaining resolution-time differences, so table-level usefulness is solid; is_ticket_unresolved is near-constant and redundant. Groundedness is generally good for extractions from short_description and original fields, but several columns over-assert specifics the terse text does not support — notably affected_scope defaulting to 'individual_user' and failure_mode inferring connection_failure for access issues — pulling groundedness down from high.
